entities.name: Chronic stable angina
observations: Exertional chest pain relieved by rest with exercise-induced ST-segment depression is consistent with chronic stable angina and inducible myocardial ischemia.

entities.name: Atenolol
observations: A beta blocker appropriate for first-line symptom control in chronic stable exertional angina.
In randomized evidence, atenolol increased exercise time and delayed development of 1-mm exercise-induced ST depression versus placebo.
Compared with diltiazem in stable angina with normal left-ventricular function, atenolol prolonged time to ST depression, reduced maximal ST depression, and reduced ambulatory ischemic episodes.

entities.name: Sublingual nitroglycerin
observations: Used primarily for rapid relief of individual angina attacks rather than long-term improvement of exercise tolerance.

entities.name: Long-acting nitrates
observations: Alternative or add-on antianginal therapy when symptoms persist or beta blockers are unsuitable.

entities.name: Amlodipine
observations: A calcium-channel blocker that can be an alternative or adjunct for persistent angina, but is not preferred over beta-blocker therapy in this scenario.

entities.name: Coronary revascularization
observations: PCI or CABG is generally reserved for refractory symptoms despite optimized medical therapy or high-risk coronary anatomy; it is not automatically first-line for uncomplicated stable angina.

entities.name: Lifestyle and risk-factor modification
observations: Smoking cessation, weight management, exercise, and risk-factor control are important for long-term cardiovascular prevention but do not substitute for direct antianginal therapy when the goal is improved exercise tolerance.

entities.name: Aspirin
observations: Important secondary prevention therapy in appropriate patients with ischemic coronary disease, but it does not directly improve exercise tolerance or suppress exertional angina.
